bindings.evidence: RB080 'YEAR OF BIRTH' as the delivery releases it, for a delivery with no age in years (prelude DEM-agecat). The canon uses agecat 'only when the survey did not collect age in years' and asks for the survey's own categories, carried as they are. The decision is the delivery's, never a row's: where any row has an age (RX010) the column is .c, 'Age categories not collected in this survey', in every row; where none has, every person gets the class (and only when every row has one: a partly filled agecat is not an output). Eurostat's disclosure rules give year of birth in 5-year classes where the age variables are 'not provided' (Malta in every operation; Germany from 2023), and code the classes differently by country and by year (a class number with a label in Malta 2021, the lowest year of the class in Malta 2025, the highest in Germany: udb_rules.json, country rules), so no age bounds are written here.
